ops.title: B1 reproduced live: cc-review could not converge from v0.20 because stop failed on an unplaced label-leaf program
ops.body:
Reproduced on Yasyfs-MacBook-Pro (yasyf-forge) 2026-08-10 against SHIPPED binaries, not a test harness.

SETUP: cc-review 0.34.0 (cask), which pins cc-interact v0.32.0 — i.e. WITHOUT the fix in 2614d0a.
A pre-0.21 cc-review daemon was live (pid 9589, started Aug 3) holding the legacy state-directory
socket, and ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.yasyf.cc-review.plist was markerless. ~/.daemonkit/bin/ held
only the v0.20-era NAME-leaf 'cc-review' (Jul 27); the LABEL-leaf 'com.yasyf.cc-review' did not exist,
because only Ensure ever places it and this machine had never ensured in the v0.21 era.

THE DEADLOCK, in three steps:
1. 'cc-review status' refuses in-place upgrade, correctly:
     daemon: a pre-0.21 daemon is running and cannot be upgraded in place;
     run "cc-review stop", then any command that starts it
2. 'cc-review stop' then fails, rc=1:
     error: daemon: stop: daemonkit: resolve program
     "/Users/yasyf/.daemonkit/bin/com.yasyf.cc-review": lstat
     /Users/yasyf/.daemonkit/bin/com.yasyf.cc-review: no such file or directory
3. The markerless plist SURVIVES. cc-review cannot converge by its own advertised path.

Escape required manual intervention a user should not need: launchctl bootout plus removing the plist
by hand. After that 'cc-review start' converged cleanly, placed the label-leaf program, and wrote a
MARKED plist naming /Users/yasyf/.daemonkit/bin/com.yasyf.cc-review; health read 'running (v0.34.0)'.

SCOPE CORRECTION, because the defect is narrower than first stated and that changes who needs the fix:
B1 bites ONLY when the label-leaf program was never placed — exclusively during a v0.20 -> v0.21
migration, before the first successful Ensure. Verified by contrast on the same machine: cc-present
(same shared Launcher, same unfixed cc-interact v0.32.0) was converged FIRST via 'start', which placed
its label-leaf binary; its subsequent 'cc-present stop' returned rc=0 and removed the plist correctly.
Steady-state Stop is unaffected. But every machine crosses the migration window exactly once, and that
is precisely when Stop is the advertised remedy — so the fix matters most for the products whose
cross-era gate TELLS the user to run stop.

CONSEQUENCE: cc-present, cc-review and cc-orchestrate each need to repin cc-interact past 2614d0a and
release before another machine migrates, or that machine hits the same deadlock. cc-patch is NOT
affected: it predates RemoveUnmarked and hand-rolls bootout + os.Remove, which is correct and must not
be "fixed" into Client.Stop.
